content: 1. Administer 0.5 mg of atropine (2 tablets) orally every 6 hours. Do not exceed a daily dose of 20 mg of diphenoxylate. Continue this regimen until initial control of diarrhea is achieved, which typically occurs within 48 hours. If diarrhea persists beyond 48 hours, contact a physician. Discontinue use if there is no clinical improvement within 10 days of using the maximum dose. 2. For maintenance therapy, reduce the daily dosage of diphenoxylate/atropine to as low as 25% of the initial daily dose. 3. Alvimopan is contraindicated in opioid-tolerant patients, defined as those who have taken therapeutic doses of opioids for more than 7 consecutive days immediately prior to alvimopan administration. Patients recently exposed to opioids may experience heightened sensitivity to alvimopan, leading to abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. 4. Avoid or use alternative drugs when combining diphenoxylate HCl with buprenorphine, butorphanol, or other opioid antagonists, as these combinations may provoke withdrawal symptoms. 5. Co-administration of diphenoxylate HCl with calcium, magnesium, potassium, or sodium oxybates can result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Reserve such combinations for patients with inadequate alternative treatment options, limit dosages and durations to the minimum required, and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 6. Cimetidine increases the effects of diphenoxylate HCl by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Co-administration of atropine with eluxadoline increases the risk of constipation-related serious adverse reactions. Avoid combining these drugs with other medications that cause constipation. 8. Glucagon increases the effects of atropine, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal adverse reactions due to additive inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Glycopyrronium tosylate topical and atropine may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Isocarboxazid increases the toxicity of diphenoxylate HCl through an unknown mechanism, posing risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by at least 14 days. 11. Linezolid increases the toxicity of diphenoxylate HCl through an unknown mechanism, with similar risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by at least 14 days. 12. Atropine may blunt the growth hormone response to macimorelin, potentially impacting diagnostic test accuracy. Allow sufficient washout time of drugs affecting growth hormone release before administering macimorelin. 13. Diphenoxylate HCl and metoclopramide intranasal may increase each other's effects. Avoid use depending on the importance of the drug to the patient. 14. Diphenoxylate HCl and olopatadine intranasal both increase sedation, leading to additive impairment of psychomotor performance and daytime functioning. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Diphenoxylate HCl and sodium oxybate both increase sedation, with risks of profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Reserve such combinations for patients with inadequate alternative treatment options, limit dosages and durations, and monitor closely. 16. Atropine decreases the effects of secretin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially causing a hyporesponse to stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least 5 half-lives before administering secretin. 17. Selegiline increases the toxicity of diphenoxylate HCl through an unknown mechanism, with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Diphenoxylate HCl and zuranolone may increase CNS depressant effects, impairing psychomotor performance. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 19. Atropine increases the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA by pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 20. Diphenoxylate HCl and benzodiazepines (e.g., alprazolam, chlordiazepoxide) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 21. Diphenoxylate HCl and CNS depressants (e.g., butalbital, amobarbital) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 22. Diphenoxylate HCl and stimulants (e.g., amphetamine, caffeine) have unclear interaction effects on sedation. Use caution and monitor. 23. Diphenoxylate HCl and anticholinergic drugs (e.g., atropine, benztropine) may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 24. Diphenoxylate HCl and opioids (e.g., buprenorphine, butorphanol) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 25. Diphenoxylate HCl and antipsychotics (e.g., chlorpromazine, aripiprazole) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 26. Diphenoxylate HCl and antihistamines (e.g., brompheniramine, chlorpheniramine) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 27. Diphenoxylate HCl and muscle relaxants (e.g., carisoprodol, chlorzoxazone) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 28. Diphenoxylate HCl and anticonvulsants (e.g., cenobamate, clobazam) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 29. Diphenoxylate HCl and other sedatives (e.g., brexanolone, brivaracetam) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 30. Diphenoxylate HCl and MAO inhibitors (e.g., phenelzine, tranylcypromine) increase toxicity, with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by at least 14 days. 31. Diphenoxylate HCl and adrenergic agonists (e.g., albuterol, arformoterol) have unclear interaction effects on sedation. Use caution and monitor. 32. Diphenoxylate HCl and other drugs with sedative properties (e.g., azelastine, baclofen) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 33. Diphenoxylate HCl and drugs with anticholinergic effects (e.g., atropine, belladonna alkaloids) may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 34. Diphenoxylate HCl and drugs affecting GI motility (e.g., bethanechol, carbachol) have unclear interaction effects. Use caution and monitor. 35. Diphenoxylate HCl and drugs with CNS depressant effects (e.g., butabarbital, butalbital) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 36. Diphenoxylate HCl and drugs with unknown interaction mechanisms (e.g., rasagiline, ropeginterferon alfa-2b) may increase neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity.
